chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who returns from a journey during the month of Ramadan, such that he sees he will enter upon his family in the forenoon or at the rising of the day. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the dawn breaks and he is outside and has not yet entered upon his family, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler returning home during Ramadan if dawn breaks before he reaches his house?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle of 'khayr' (choice) for a traveler who returns home after Fajr but before sunset, distinguishing this state from one where the fast is already obligatory. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the obligation of fasting is contingent upon being present in one's residence at the time of dawn, allowing flexibility for those transitioning from travel. This nuance underscores the practical ease (taysir) granted to travelers in Shia fiqh compared to stricter interpretations found in other schools.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rafa’at Bin Musa who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who comes back from a journey during a Month of Ramazan, so he sees that he has come over to his family in the morning or at the rising of the day. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the dawn emerges and he is outside and has not yet come to his family, so he is with the choice, if he so desires to Fasts, and if he so desires to, he breaks’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rifa’ah ibn Musa who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who comes home from a journey in the month of Ramadan until he can see that he is about to arrive home at noon or when the day is high. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is dawn and he has not yet arrived in his family, it then is up to him to fast or not to fast.’”
